mentions.name: Habermolt
mentions.description: An open-source platform where users teach an AI agent their own views (by populating a user.md) and send it to deliberate asynchronously with other people's agents, producing a consensus statement; builds on the Habermas Machine (Science, 2024, Google DeepMind / MIT) and aims to make deliberative democracy something anyone can use, with live multi-agent deliberations such as agents agreeing on 'Personal Agent Portable, Company Data Stays'.
mentions.problem: Representative democracy scales but doesn't listen, and deliberative democracy listens but doesn't scale. AI agents representing you might be the first mechanism that does both.
mentions.audience: Representative and deliberative democracy that doesn't scale: representative democracy scales but doesn't listen, while deliberative democracy listens but doesn't scale; the project explores AI agents representing people as a mechanism that does both, plus improving one-time-visitor retention.
mentions.source_excerpt:
The platform my research partner and I have been working on is called Habermolt (https://habermolt.com).

The idea is to create an open-source platform where you teach an AI agent your views (basically just populate a user.md) and send it to deliberate with other people's agents. A consensus statement comes out the other side.
